subject: How to set different background colors in the same plot

messages.author: 75db403eb2b8ba68
messages.subject: How to set different background colors in the same plot
parts:
I have decided to learn ggplot- so therefore this; my first post in
the dedicated ggplot2 group.

I would like to reproduce something similar to this (QOLI report by
M.Frisch): http://wana.dk/wp-content/uploads/2009/05/plot_to_reproduce.png

But how? - Below what I got so far for one of them.

# The data
Health <- -4#
Self-esteem <- -6#
Self_esteem <- -6#
Goals_Values <- 4#
Money <- -3#
Children <- 0#
test <- data.frame(Self_esteem,Goals_Values,Money,Children)#
row.names(test) <- "score"#
t1 <- melt(test)#

# Draw the plot
ggplot(data=t1,aes(x=value,y=variable))+
scale_x_continuous("Score",limits=c(-6,6),breaks=c(-3.5,-0.5,0.5))+
scale_y_discrete("Dimension")+
geom_point()+
opts(panel.background=theme_rect(fill="red"))+
opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_line(NA))

panel.background is most likely the wrong way forward - but what would
be the right way? I have thought about plotting vertical lines - but
that doesn't seam very elegant.

I haven't even begun working on the other barplot-type. But I guess
that will be simple when to question mentioned in the subject is
solved.

Cheers

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: How to set different background colors in the same plot
parts:
On Sat, May 9, 2009 at 9:47 AM, achristoffersen
<achrist...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I would like to reproduce something similar to this (QOLI report by
> M.Frisch): http://wana.dk/wp-content/uploads/2009/05/plot_to_reproduce.png

You can use geom_rect for backgrounds as shown in section 5.10 of the
ggplot book.

Something like this:

df <- data.frame(
    Domain = factor(rev(c("Health","Self-Esteem","Goals &
Values","Money","Work","Play")),ordered=TRUE),
    Satisfaction = c(  -4, -6, 4, -3, -2, -2 ) )

ggplot(df) +
 geom_rect(aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),xmin=-6.5,xmax=-3
,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.3)) +
 geom_rect(aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),xmin=-3
,xmax=-0.5,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.5)) +
 geom_rect(aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),xmin=-0.5,xmax=
0.5,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.7)) +
 xlim(-6,6) +
 geom_point(data=df,aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),size=5,shape=15)

Hope this helps,

         -s

> appreciated:
> I would like to have horisontal gridlines shown. But I can't find the
> command to  show only horizontal grid-lines (I guess showing only
> horizontal grid-lines, would be a contradiction in terms, since it
> then wouldn't be a grid). Anyways: Grid-lines is drawn below the
> rectangles. So I tried using alpha for making the grid-lines visible.
> But this gives a non-uniform look to the plot. Therefore I would like
> to use geom_hline. But this simpel geom I can't figure out. What ever
> I do - the line is drawn at the bottom of the plot.
You need to use xintercept and yintercept.

> Finaly: I cant figure out how to put a second annotated yaxis on the
> plot (some people like this). Also: I haven't got around to putting
> labels above each rectangle like the linked png from my previous post.
> I suspect I can approximate something nice with title but pointeres
> are more than welcome.
You can't currently do either of these things easily in ggplot2.

> final and last - Is there a smarter way, whereby I can plot all the
> rectangles in one go? From HAdleys book chapter 5.10 this should be
> possible (and as of now I haven't given it much trial and error time).

Here's one attempt:

bg <- data.frame(
start = c(-6.5, -3, -0.5, 0.5),
end = c(-3, -0.5, 0.5, 6.5),
fill = grey(c(0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.8))
)

ggplot(df) +
# Background rectangles
geom_rect(data = bg, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, fill = fill),
ymin = 0, ymax = 7) +
# Grid lines
geom_hline(yintercept = 1:6, colour = "white") +
geom_vline(xintercept = seq(-6, 6), colour = "white") +
# Data points
geom_point(aes(Satisfaction, Domain), size = 3, shape = 15) +
# Set expand to c(0,0) so that there's no gap between axis and data
scale_x_continuous("Domain", limits=c(-6.5,6.5), expand = c(0,0)) +
# Have to manually specify that the y axis is discrete because the
# first layer pretends it is continuous
scale_y_discrete("Satisfaction") +
# Just treat the background fill as a fill - don't scale it
scale_fill_identity() +
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())

It should be easier to do this sort of thing though. I'll have a
think about it.
